citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
The licensee has a formal arrangement with an attending veterinarian and a written Program of Veterinary Care but does
not have arrangements for the Attending Veterinarian (AV) to conduct regularly scheduled visits to the premises. The
licensee provided a Program of Veterinary Care with the space documenting the frequency of the regularly scheduled
visits by the veterinarian that states the visits will be conducted on an annual basis. The Attending Veterinarian has not
conducted a site visit at the current facility according to the facility representative.
Without the required regularly scheduled visits to the premises, the AV cannot effectively ensure the provision of
adequate veterinary care and the health and well-being of the animals housed at the facility.
Each dealer and exhibitor shall employ an attending veterinarian under formal arrangements. In the case of a part-time
attending veterinarian or consultant arrangements, the formal arrangements shall include a written program of veterinary
care and regularly scheduled visits to the premises of the dealer or exhibitor.
Correct by 15-July-2026

citations.desc: Primary enclosures used to transport nonhuman primates.
citations.narrative:
The facility did not contain one non-human primate in a primary enclosure during transit. APHIS Officials were present at
the facility when the animals returned from a public exhibition event and did not observe the animals being removed from
the transportation vehicle in a primary enclosure. When inquiring with the facility representative on how the animals were
transported to the event the representative stated the younger spider monkey “Sophia” stays in a shoulder pouch worn by
the representative and not contained within an enclosure. The second spider monkey “Caesar” was transported in a wire
crate type enclosure that was shown to APHIS officials.
Failure to transport an animal in a primary enclosure could cause stress, injury, or even death if the vehicle is involved in
an accident. Any person subject to the Animal Welfare regulations must not transport or deliver for transport in commerce
a nonhuman primate unless it is contained in a primary enclosure, such as a compartment, transport cage, carton, or
crate. The transport enclosure must meet all requirements set forth in this subpart.
Correct by 16-June-2026.

citations.desc: Primary enclosures used to transport nonhuman primates.
citations.narrative:
The transport enclosure being used does not prevent the primate from putting parts of its body outside of the enclosure.
APHIS officials were present at the facility when the licensee was returning home from an exhibition event. When
inquiring with the facility representative on how the animals were transported to the event the representative stated that
the spider monkey “Caesar” was transported in a wire crate type enclosure that was shown to APHIS officials. Nonhuman
primates that can put body parts through openings in the sides/doors of their transport crates may become injured during
transport or may injure nearby animals. Correct for all future transports by using only crates that prevent the animals from
putting their body parts outside of the crate. Correct by 19-June-2026.

citations.desc: Primary enclosures used to transport nonhuman primates.
citations.narrative:
The transport enclosure being used for one spider monkey did not have projecting rims. APHIS officials were present at
the facility when the licensee was returning home from an exhibition event. When inquiring with the facility representative
on how the animals were transported to the event the representative stated that the spider monkey “Caesar” was
transported in a wire crate type enclosure that was shown to APHIS officials. The lack of projecting rims can cause
inadequate ventilation when something is placed against the enclosure. Projecting rims or similar devices must be located
on the exterior of each enclosure wall having a ventilation opening, in order to prevent obstruction of the openings. The
projecting rims or similar devices must be large enough to provide a minimum air circulation space of 0.75 inches
between the primary enclosure and anything the enclosure is placed against. The licensee must ensure that the transport
enclosure has appropriate projecting rims. Correct by 19-June-2026.

citations.desc: Primary enclosures used to transport nonhuman primates.
citations.narrative:
One spider monkey transported in an enclosure that did not have the words “Live Animal” or “Wild Animals” with arrows or
other markings indicating the correct upright position of the enclosure clearly marked. APHIS officials were present at the
facility when the licensee was returning home from an exhibition event. When inquiring with the facility representative on
how the animals were transported to the event the representative stated that the spider monkey “Caesar” was transported
in a wire crate type enclosure that was shown to APHIS officials. A lack of clear markings can inhibit correct handling and
cage orientation by first responders in the event of an emergency. The licensee must ensure that on top and on one or
more sides are marked with the words “Wild Animals” or “Live Animals” in letters at least 1 inch (2.5 cm) high, with arrows
or other markings to indicate the correct upright position of the primary enclosure. Correct by 19-June-2026.
This inspection and exit interview were conducted with a Facility Representative.
Additional Inspectors:
Eric Irvin, VETERINARY MEDICAL OFFICER n
